DISCUSSION
Transformers change voltage and current levels, but POWER IN always equals POWER OUT. Transformers do not generate power, they transfer power.
The power transfer is from a power source to a load or from one circuit to another.

Es depends on Ep, Np, and Ns: Es - secondary voltage
Assuming no losses, if Ns equals Np (number of turns of secondary and primary), then Es equals Ep (voltage on secondary and primary).

TRANSFORMER LOSSES - Transformers are not perfect. Some power is lost between the primary and secondary coils.
DEFINITION
COPPER LOSS - Copper losses occur when current flows in a conductor. All conductors have some resistance and when current flows power is consumed as heat just like a resistor.
DEFINITION

EDDY CURRENT LOSS - Eddy current losses occur because of the fluctuating magnetic field. AC current generates random current in the iron core and this eddy current is dissipated as power in the form of heat. Air core transformers do not have eddy current losses.
DEFINITION
HYSTERESIS LOSS - Hysteresis loss occurs when the magnetic field is reversed. Power is consumed in reversing the magnetic field each time the direction of current changes.

Transformers can, however, reverse the phase of the applied AC voltage or sine wave. This is called phase inversion.
